requirement: R27 composition DAG: move one owner construction without behaviour change

owner.rationale: Smallest owner: a stateless ordered stage runner (pending/run are the existing pure session-bootstrap functions). It has no network, state ownership, port or store; the host only held one state variable and one call. Backend is the whole runtime and cannot move without a large extraction.
owner.dagConstruction: composition-dag.ts: bootstrapLayer supplies pending/run; composeBootstrapOwner() builds CompositionLayer once; bootstrapOwner is the singleton instance. bootstrapLayer is the only construction site; index.ts no longer imports createPendingBootstrapState/runSessionBootstrapStages.
owner.hostUse: src/index.ts:20773 selects composedBootstrapOwner; :30152 pending(); :34584 run(handlers). The host still sets the running state before awaiting, preserving the observable intermediate state.

escapeHatch.inert: Both are optional and unused in production; production always uses the DAG singleton. They exist only so the identity test can observe the host calling the owner's methods.
escapeHatch.removal: Delete both option fields and pass the composed owner through the future public composition result (or expose backend.composition); the host keeps using the DAG owner with no call-site change.

remainingOwners.blocker: createRuntimeBridgeBackend is the whole host backend (options, network, fixtures, stores); extracting a service boundary is a large design step, not a construction move.
startBridgeServer binds the listener and owns routes/lifecycle; needs an explicit server owner plus shutdown/readiness ordering.
refresh/reload is embedded in backend closures and shared mutable state; needs a read/write handoff contract and atomic publication.
shutdown/drain spans backend, supervisor, queues and vendor children; needs the R27 partial-shutdown order and finalizer ownership.
benchmark execution is a separate CLI/runner; cancellation/overlap isolation and cross-process ownership are not modelled by the DAG.
cli.ts is the process entrypoint (args/SEA/startup); it is not a runtime service and needs packaging decisions.
shape only; not connected to real provider execution. Needs the provider dispatch seam and reviewed concurrency defaults.
DAG names shapes; the real stores retain their own PRAGMAs/owners. Wiring them crosses the storage ownership boundary and R28/R30 contracts.
